blocks.x: Federated learning across hospital networks, model training across 17 sites with zero patient-data movement and the ethics board's public endorsement

A national medical research institute: Education institutions feel technology failures at enrolment and results time, when volume spikes and patience does not. The Achala program started with the peak load —. The baseline signed in week two made the cost visible in units the finance team already owns, and the engagement ran under the standard Achala charter — a named metric, a named control owner and gates that evidence every move.

The baseline negotiation measured the deadlock: data-sharing agreements stalling at site 4 of 40, model development limited to one pilot hospital's cohort, and reviewers questioning the model's generalization because it had seen one region's patients.
Central pooling was never going to clear ethics. The science needed the diversity; the governance needed the guarantees.

We built the federated spine: training runs executed at each site with only model updates, never patient data, crossing the boundary, aggregation under cryptographic attestation each site can verify, site-level contribution and bias metrics reported openly, and the ethics documentation generated from the protocol rather than written around it. Four sites became seventeen; the board endorsed publicly.
